decks.name: LeetCode #235 - Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
decks.description: Find the lowest common ancestor of two nodes in a binary search tree

cards.question: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree: Given a binary search tree (BST), find the lowest common ancestor (LCA) node of two given nodes in the BST. According to the definition of LCA: The lowest common ancestor is defined between two nodes p and q as the lowest node in the tree that has both p and q as descendants (where we allow a node to be a descendant of itself).

solutions.name: Recursion
solutions.explanation: Leverage BST property where left subtree values are less than root and right subtree values are greater. If both p and q values are less than current node, LCA must be in left subtree. If both greater, LCA in right subtree. Otherwise, current node is the split point and thus the LCA. Recursive solution with O(h) time and space.

solutions.exampleWalkthrough: Given BST [6,2,8,0,4,7,9] with p=2, q=8: Start at 6. min(2,8)=2 < 6 and max(2,8)=8 > 6, so 6 is between p and q values. Return 6 as LCA since it's the split point.

solutions.name: Iteration
solutions.explanation: Iterative approach using BST property without recursion. Start at root and traverse down. If both p and q values are greater than current, go right. If both less, go left. Otherwise, current node is the split point and thus the LCA. Optimal O(h) time with O(1) space, no recursion overhead.
